first_look.question: Do the bouncing and hopping motions fall the way they should in Moon gravity?

scene_card.scene: Grey dusty ground under a black sky with two bulky-suited figures and a planted flag; foreground figure hopping.

first_look.summary: Two bulky-suited figures bounce and hop beside a planted flag on grey dusty ground under a black sky. The foreground figure makes clearly separated two-footed hops around 8 s and 11 s; fitting the fall of both hops tests whether the motion is lunar.

checks.what: downward acceleration during free flight of the foreground figure's larger two-footed hops
checks.why: a body with nothing holding it up must accelerate downward at the local gravity, so the fitted fall directly tests whether the motion is lunar

wonder.claim: Two bulky-suited figures bounce and hop beside a planted flag on grey dusty ground under a black sky on the Moon.
wonder.not_realistic_if: It is not realistic if the fitted downward acceleration is near Earth gravity or the airtime is too short for the measured hop height.
wonder.realistic_if: It is realistic if the hops show long floaty airtime and the fitted downward acceleration matches lunar gravity within error.
